description: Team Neutrino is passionate about space science, Earth observation, and data science. We aim to turn NASA's Earth data into meaningful insights using programming, machine learning, and visualization. We're looking for enthusiastic teammates skilled in Python, web development, GIS, and research to build innovative solutions and understand our changing planet.
summary:
We developed an interactive web-based platform for exploring and analysing real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations. The platform brings multiple stages of astronomical data exploration into one unified interface. Users can search for celestial objects by name or coordinates, explore available observations, view processed FITS images, and examine observations over time using timeline and blink visualization. It also provides image comparison tools, observation metadata, data quality information, and provenance details. Additionally, a candidate review section supports the investigation of potentially interesting signals through human validation.
Our project addresses the challenge of making complex astronomical observations easier to access, visualize, compare and investigate. By combining scientific data visualization with quality assessment and candidate investigation, it helps users understand both the observations and their limitations. This is important because it makes real SPHEREx data more accessible and supports further scientific exploration of the infrared universe.
details:
Our project is an interactive web-based platform designed to explore, visualize and analyse real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations. It aims to make complex astronomical data easier to access, understand and investigate through a unified scientific exploration platform.

The platform allows users to search for celestial objects using their names or astronomical coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination). Target names are resolved into coordinates, which are then used to retrieve relevant SPHEREx observations from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA).

On the backend, the system handles astronomical data retrieval and FITS image processing, including image preparation, coordinate mapping using World Coordinate System (WCS) information, metadata extraction and data quality assessment. It also supports the identification and investigation of potentially interesting signals through candidate detection and review workflows.

The frontend, developed using React.js, JavaScript, CSS and Vite, provides an interactive interface with several integrated features:

- Search the Sky: Search celestial targets by name or coordinates.

- Image Viewer: Explore processed SPHEREx images and available observations.

- Timeline & Blink: View observations sequentially to examine changes across observations.

- Image Comparison: Compare selected observations and examine differences where scientifically compatible.

- Metadata & Provenance: Inspect observation details, processing information, data quality and source information.

- Candidate Review: Investigate potential signals and support human validation of interesting candidates.

The project benefits researchers and astronomy enthusiasts by simplifying access to real infrared observations and bringing data exploration, visualization, comparison and investigation into one connected workflow.

Its intended impact is to support the scientific exploration of the infrared universe, improve accessibility to astronomical datasets and help users understand the reliability and limitations of observations.

The project is creative in the way it combines astronomical data retrieval, scientific image processing, interactive visualization, temporal exploration and candidate investigation into a single SPHEREx-focused platform. We also considered scientific accuracy, data reliability, image compatibility, usability and transparency of data provenance throughout development.

Technologies and tools: React.js, JavaScript, CSS, Vite, Python-based backend processing, REST APIs, NASA/IPAC IRSA, CDS Sesame, FITS astronomical data and WCS coordinate information.
